title: SpringBoot
label: SpringBoot
desc: An opinionated Spring platform that auto-configures a production-ready Java service around plain Spring components.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Generate a project from start.spring.io, then run it with the bundled wrapper.

snippets.code:
# Generate a Maven project with the starters used in this sheet
curl -fsSL https://start.spring.io/starter.tgz \
  -d type=maven-project \
  -d language=java \
  -d bootVersion=3.5.0 \
  -d javaVersion=21 \
  -d groupId=com.example \
  -d artifactId=catalog \
  -d dependencies=web,data-jpa,validation,actuator,flyway,postgresql \
  | tar -xz

# Start the app on port 8080 with the Maven wrapper
cd catalog
./mvnw spring-boot:run

# Build the executable jar and run it on its own
./mvnw clean package
java -jar target/catalog-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar

# Override any property from the command line
java -jar target/catalog-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar --server.port=9000 --spring.profiles.active=local

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3.5.0</version>
    <relativePath/>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
  <artifactId>catalog</artifactId>
  <version>0.0.1-SNAPSHOT</version>

  <properties>
    <java.version>21</java.version>
  </properties>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-data-jpa</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-validation</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-database-postgresql</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
      <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

sections.title: Project Structure
sections.description: Package by feature so each slice holds its own entity, repository, service and controller.

snippets.code:
catalog/
  pom.xml
  mvnw
  src/
    main/
      java/com/example/catalog/
        CatalogApplication.java        # @SpringBootApplication entry point
        product/
          Product.java                 # JPA entity
          ProductRepository.java       # Spring Data interface
          ProductService.java          # Transactional business rules
          ProductController.java       # HTTP layer
          ProductRequest.java          # Validated input record
          ProductResponse.java         # Output record
        config/
          CatalogProperties.java       # Typed configuration
          SecurityConfiguration.java
        common/
          ApiExceptionHandler.java     # @RestControllerAdvice
      resources/
        application.yml                # Default configuration
        db/migration/
          V1__create_product.sql       # Flyway owns the schema
    test/
      java/com/example/catalog/
        product/
          ProductControllerTest.java
          ProductServiceTest.java

sections.title: Database
sections.description: Connect to PostgreSQL, let Flyway migrate and Hibernate only validate.

snippets.code:
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/catalog
    username: catalog
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
    hikari:
      maximum-pool-size: 10
      connection-timeout: 3000
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
    properties:
      hibernate:
        jdbc:
          time_zone: UTC
  flyway:
    enabled: true
    locations: classpath:db/migration

-- src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_product.sql
create table product (
    id          bigserial primary key,
    name        varchar(120) not null unique,
    price_cents bigint       not null check (price_cents > 0),
    stock       integer      not null check (stock >= 0),
    version     bigint       not null default 0,
    created_at  timestamptz  not null default now()
);

create index idx_product_stock on product (stock);

-- Flyway records this file in flyway_schema_history and never re-runs it

# Local PostgreSQL 16 with the credentials used by application.yml
docker run --name catalog-db \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=catalog \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=catalog \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  -d postgres:16

# Inspect which migrations were applied
docker exec catalog-db \
  psql -U catalog -d catalog -c "select version, description, success from flyway_schema_history;"

# Run the app against this database
DB_PASSWORD=secret ./mvnw spring-boot:run

sections.title: Actuator
sections.description: Expose health and metrics endpoints and add a domain health check.

snippets.code:
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,metrics
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: when-authorized
      probes:
        enabled: true
  info:
    env:
      enabled: true

info:
  app:
    name: catalog
    version: 0.0.1

# Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes
curl -s localhost:8080/actuator/health/liveness
curl -s localhost:8080/actuator/health/readiness

# Full health tree, details only for an authenticated caller
curl -s -u ana:s3cret-pass localhost:8080/actuator/health

# Available metric names, then one specific metric
curl -s -u ana:s3cret-pass localhost:8080/actuator/metrics | jq -r '.names[]' | head -20
curl -s -u ana:s3cret-pass localhost:8080/actuator/metrics/http.server.requests | jq '.measurements'
